utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Karic. I hope you had a good rest.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. You have five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Just one point of information. Does Rule 15 bis apply when you don't have the reserve Judge sitting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for your reminder. We're sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, with Judge Flavia Lattanzi being away due to her personal urgent matters. Thank you, Mr. Robinson. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Karic.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karic, who beat you at Pale, out of the people you know?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this man, Kusic, I don't know what his first name is. I didn't know really know him. I knew him a bit, and then I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He is no longer alive; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not the one. This is another one, a younger one. It's not Rajko Kusic. It's a younger one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the guards did not beat you, so he wasn't a guard; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who a guard was, who was a guard. I couldn't see anyone, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Karic, that this Fehim Hrvo lost his life at a check-point because he did not want to stop because he had an automatic rifle and a hand-grenade in his car?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this other one had a heart attack and that he died in the operating room?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which other one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said the three died?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And he didn't die of a heart attack. He died of the beatings. They were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was Braco Paradzina, what office did he hold, the one who cautioned you to seek shelter?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know before the war, he had his own transportation business. I don't know what he was then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was not an official in the municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about Centrotrans; who was this Mico Danojlovic, what did he do there?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in Sarajevo, in a warehouse in Centrotrans. When the war broke out, he was sort of a boss, he was sort of the guy in charge. I don't know what to call him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, a warehouse worker was the boss. Did he have the authority to dismiss you?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he had the authority to do that, but he told me not to come anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you said that for a while you did not go out because they started arresting Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, this Nasko Smajic, who died of a heart attack, you say he did not die of a heart attack?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, heart attack? They beat him black and blue. They killed him by beating him. They were beaten with rifle-butts, sticks, they kicked them. They did all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're going to ask for medical documentation, sir. We're going to ask for Pale to inform us about everything. Let me put this to you, Mr. Karic, saying how things actually were: You had close relations with your brother-in-law, Ibro, and that is where you sought shelter when Paradzina told you to leave before things calmed down. Then they called you to come to work. Then you worked. Then you were transferred to the ticket office, because there was more work at the ticket office because of the large number of refugees. Then you heard of this operation on the 22nd of May in Renovica. Then you were hiding until the 30th of May because you knew that you were linked to Ibro, and then you were arrested; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is not right from amongst all of this?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you say, that you were -- that I was linked to Ibro, that he was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, may I make a suggestion. You're now putting your case to the witness, are you not? Now, I would suggest that as you put one suggestion, you give him a chance to answer yea or nay. He answers. Then you put another one. And so at the end of the day, he will have answered all the suggestions, and not just the last one. I would suggest this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. But, again, it's due to time. All my mistakes are due to a lack of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So all the things up to Ibro, you thought all the other things were right; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I was hiding. I simply couldn't walk around. I was afraid to go out. I had no reason to hide. I had no reason to think that -- well, a person is afraid. You hear all sorts of things, you hear all sorts of bad things. And what you claim, that I was hiding at Ibro's and went to Ibro, first of all, I wasn't staying with Ibro. I was staying with my father-in-law and mother-in-law. What you're saying that some kind of thing happened, I don't know about that because that happened after all of that. I don't know. You're accusing me of something that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, we'll take it slowly. You went to work. You passed by Serb check-points, they checked your ID, and they let you go after the car would be checked; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean when I was coming from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when you went to Sokolac.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you went to Sokolac and when you went to Renovica; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Serb drivers brought you food?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that happened once. And it wasn't a driver, it was a conductor, but it's all the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: People who were not in authority and not in government, Paradzina and then later on this Miso Danojlovic, advised you to get away, to seek shelter, and then after that, two or three days later, they called you to come back to work; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you saw and heard that the operation in Renovica was underway on the 22nd of May. Until then, you worked normally; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't exactly normal, but I was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see and hear that there was this operation underway in Renovica?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some people setting out, but I said what Lazar said yesterday. It's not that I realised where they were going and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After that, from the 22nd of May until the 30th of May, you did not go to work; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 30th of May, you were arrested, you were brought into custody, and you made a statement on the 31st of May; right?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not that I gave a statement. It was just along the way, in the camp, when this man just asked me a few questions. It was just a few sentences. It was no statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, there was fighting in Praca, Bogovici, and in other Muslim villages that had surrendered weapons?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you were in this cultural centre, in prison, where 28 Muslims were brought in, fighters from Renovica, and you say 60, and then you say 150 to 200?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained that to you yesterday. 100, 200, 300, it doesn't really matter at all, and I don't know that. And all of those who were brought in, they were brought in before me, that is to say, the 22nd, and I was brought in on the 30th. First of all, they were not fighters or soldiers; they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At line 15, the witness said that as far as he knew, there was not any fighting in the villages where had handed over their weapons, and that's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I know? I'm not interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Praca was returned to the Muslims after the war and that they formed the municipality of Pale, Praca?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened afterwards, after the war, so this division of sorts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, now it's for you to put your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Kula, nobody beat you, and at least once you reported to go out to work. And you were taken there kindly because better food was received there, as well as cigarettes and tobacco, just like other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How was it?

utterances.speaker: HAJRUDIN KARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not report for that. This man, this sergeant, took me there, I don't know, to have an egg or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Mr. Hayden.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYDEN
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karic, that concludes your evidence. On behalf of the Tribunal and the Bench, I thank you for your coming again all the way to The Hague to give it. We appreciate it very much. You are free now to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who is the next witness, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The next witness, Mr. President, will be Nebojsa Ristic, and we'll be calling this witness viva voce, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's bring in the witness. And your estimate of time for your direct is ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It remains one hour and a half, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ristic. Please make yourself comfortable, please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you state your full name for the record, please?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: My name is Nebojsa Ristic. My father's name is Cedomir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: The 9th of January, 1972.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is your nationality?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Serb, Orthodox.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What was your occupation in the period between mid-April 1992 until the end of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I worked on the security detail of the president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was there a slight change in your duties in mid-1994?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, up until mid-1994, I worked on providing security for the buildings where the president and his family were staying. And from mid-1994, I was only in charge of his personal security.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Who was your formal employer during that entire period?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Up until May 1992, I was an employee of the Serb Democratic Party. I worked on the security of the president of the party, the SDS, and their buildings. And from May 1992, when the MUP was established, I was an employee of the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska in the State Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus on the locations where President Karadzic lived and worked during the period April 1992 until the end of the conflict. First of all, could you explain to the Court, where did President Karadzic live from April 1992 until late 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: President Karadzic lived or resided with his family at two locations between April 1992 and the end of the conflict in 1995. The first location was at the Panorama Hotel complex, or to be precise, there was a weekend cottage above the hotel complex that we referred to as Villa Sipad. The second location was a family home at the other end of Pale in a place called Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: When, approximately, did President Karadzic move his residence from Villa Sipad to Krivace?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to focus now on the locations where the president worked while he was in Pale. Could you tell Their Honours where he worked in Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: At the time between 1992 and 1993, the president's office was at three locations. The first one was in a building called Kikinda. Then, at the end of 1992, the office was relocated to the Panorama complex of buildings, to a building called Mali Dom. Finally, in 1994 it was relocated to the administrative building of the Famos factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was his -- were his offices located at Famos until the end of the conflict from 1994?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, until the end of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to clarify your earlier answer. You said between 1992 and 1993, the president's office was in three locations. Did you mean to say between 1992 and 1995, the president's office was in three locations?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies. That's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn to the Villa Sipad. Were you -- during your duties guarding the Villa Sipad, were you based in the villa, itself, or in a different building?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: While I was performing my duties, I was at the building, itself. Otherwise, when I was off duty, I was always nearby, within the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And where in the building were you based, and where did the president and his family sleep?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I had a room in the Hotel Panorama, whereas the president and his family were residing at the facility that I secured; namely, Villa Sipad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, within the Villa Sipad, could you tell Their Honours, briefly, the communications facilities that were available that you saw there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: At the Villa Sipad, we had a telephone line, a radio set, and there was a military telephone line there, a field telephone set.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was there any back-up electricity generator at the Villa Sipad?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you happen to know how it worked or whether there was fuel for it? Do you happen to know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Power cuts were quite frequent during that period of time, and these generators would switch on automatically whenever it happened. As for how they were fueled, I truly don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, after President Karadzic and his family moved to the house at Krivace, did the electricity generator remain at Villa Sipad?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I think that the generator was also moved to the house at Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you personally act as a courier at Villa Sipad?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: My sole duty was that of a security detail, though whenever it was necessary for me to deliver something to a certain location, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Were there others who performed courier duties at Villa Sipad?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were people assigned to that duty, since they were couriers working for the president's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know the Republic Communications Centre in Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did the couriers ever take communications to or from the Republic Communications Centre?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: They would convey messages. There was communication between the centre and the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, President Momcilo Krajisnik, the president of the Assembly, where was he living during this period?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: He also lived in the Hotel Panorama complex.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And Ms. Biljana Plavsic, where did she live?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: She would come to Pale occasionally and had a place to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't catch your last answer there, Mr. Ristic. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Ms. Biljana Plavsic also had her rooms at the Hotel Panorama complex, but she was there more rarely than the president of the Assembly, the speaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I request 65 ter 2021, and if we could go to page 8 of that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you recognise this building that's circled?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: This is the building where the president stayed with his family from late 1993 onwards. This is the building at Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is that your handwriting at the top of the photograph with the date, 19th February 2009?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we go to page 9 of this same 65 ter number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is that building?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I think it's the same building, it's the same house at Krivace where the president stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you mark on this photograph the points marked "1" and the two points marked "2"?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you explain what those points refer to?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Under "1" is the house where the security personnel stayed. That was our base. My colleagues and I stayed there. Under "2" are the houses that the MUP forces used to secure the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Within the house, itself, do you know what communications facilities were present there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I do know that they had recourse to telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to the first page of this same exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At the top, we see some words and the date and a signature. Is that your handwriting and is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is this building?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: It's the Kikinda building where the office of the president of Republika Srpska was housed initially.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you know any of President Karadzic's staff who worked at this building? No need to give names.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know how communications would reach the president while he was at work at this building?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, it was standard procedure. You -- the messages would reach the president's secretary, and she would convey them further.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we go to the next -- sorry, to the third page of this exhibit, please. We see some writing in the middle of this photograph. Perhaps we could zoom in a little bit on the right-hand part of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And if you could tell us what that building is, Mr. Ristic, please.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: This is Mali Dom, part of the Panorama complex. This was the place where the president's office was housed after it was moved from the Kikinda building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a little further on that building, Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What floor was the president's cabinet --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, not the circled building, Mr. Registrar. It's the building -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, on that building on the screen in front of you with the arrow pointing towards it, on what floor was the president's cabinet?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: On the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Who was based on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: This was where the office of the president of the National Assembly was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And who was based on the top floor?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: There were offices of the vice-presidents of the republic, Mr. Koljevic and Madam Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know how communication would reach this particular building?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, mainly over the telephone and by way of the courier service.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've told us already that this building was within the Panorama Hotel complex; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And did the Panorama Hotel complex have a back-up electricity generator?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we move, please, to page 7 of this exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, the next location of the president's office that was within the compound of the Famos factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On this photograph, we see writing at the top indicating this is Famos, and we see a number of figures on the photograph. Did you mark this photograph, yourself?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we zoom in on the building with all the figures on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you explain what "X" denotes?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, the place where the president's office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And just briefly for Their Honours, could you run through what "1," "2," "3," "5," "6," and "7" refer to?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: "1" is the entrance. "2" is the back door. "3" is the offices where we were staying. "4," you cannot see it here, is the entrance into the compound; that is where the barrier is as well. Then "5" is the restaurant where -- where the security people had their meals. Then "6" is the other restaurant for guests and -- I mean clients, guests. The president had his meals there and all the officials. "7" is the building that was used as a school or the university. I don't know which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: How would communications reach the president's office within the Famos complex?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, it was by telephone, PTT lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Were you personally responsible for taking incoming calls and dealing with outgoing communications by telephone?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did this Famos complex have access to its own electricity back-up generators?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we zoom out back to the original size, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think we see number 4 on this photograph. Now, Mr. Ristic, could you just remind us what number 4 denotes?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, the entrance into the compound. That is where the barrier was and also the desk, the entrance desk.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end, the very end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, in particular the last part of your answer, please, for the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a fence, a wall around the rest of the factory. You couldn't enter the compound anywhere else but there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we move now to page 6 of this exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What is the set of buildings we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, also like the previous photograph, the Famos factory compound, but from a different vantage point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you, with a pen, mark something to the -- on the left part of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What did you mark there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I marked the building that was used by the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you ever see any persons in military uniform at the Famos complex?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Since it was the Ministry of Defence that was there, there were uniformed persons there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, the Trial Chamber has heard evidence that President Karadzic was also the supreme commander of the army. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Are you aware of any meetings that took place in Pale with senior military figures?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you describe, more or less, how often such meetings would take place?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say exactly, but I know that more often there were meetings in the beginning, that is to say, in 1992 and 1993. Afterwards, it was less frequently. I don't know, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the military figures who would attend those high-level meetings?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you just give us a few names of who would come, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, these were people who made up the Supreme Command, I mean, highly-positioned officers of Republika Srpska who had different duties. They all came. I really wouldn't want to single anyone out. Well, anyway, they did come.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I'd like to tender 65 ter 21021.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, I would like those markings and legend to be interpreted. In particular, I saw page 5, this drawing done by the witness, and all are written in Cyrillic. I think it would be better off if we had translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I believe we've up-loaded a translation of most parts of this exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But still --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We will make sure that that is done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI P2841, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I now call up, please, 65 ter 23169. This is a map of Pale, dating from approximately 1994, prepared by the Government of the United States.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: When this map comes up, Mr. Ristic, if you could see if you could find the Panorama complex on it. Do you see the Panorama complex?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to take a pen, with the assistance of the Usher, and mark six locations on this map, simply put a circle at each location and then a figure. Now, if you could circle the Panorama complex and put down "1."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait until you're assisted by the Usher. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you circle the Panorama complex and put down the figure "1"?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Circle the Famos complex and put down the figure "2."

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark the direction of the Kikinda complex?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. I think this is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you put down the figure "3" there, please?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is the house at Krivace on this map?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you just indicate approximately where it was, in terms of direction?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. It's in this direction, somewhere around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you put down a "5" there, please?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: I think that should be "4," Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Indeed. We can use "4" for the next one. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: For the Republican Communications Centre, and as far as you're able to tell, could you circle its approximate location and put down the figure "4"?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Number 4 for the Republic Communications Centre.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Very well. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Finally, could you put down Dom Kulture and mark "6," please?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you put your signature and date at the bottom of the map, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Today is the 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2842, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to a separate topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic, do you know the name Miroslav Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: He was a civilian official in the party, the Serb Democratic Party, in the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did he ever come to visit President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you give the Court a general picture of how often he would come to Bratunac to visit the president -- sorry, how often he would come to Pale to visit the president?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, he came maybe more than others. Well, not a lot more, not a lot less. He did come. He was maybe in this group that visited the president more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, if you could ask the witness how he did know Mr. Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you answer that, please, Mr. Witness? How did you know Mr. Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, by virtue of the fact that he came there. We were duty-bound to know who was coming to see the president. I don't know how it was that I found out that it was actually Mr. Deronjic the first time. Probably, I heard that from my colleagues or from the secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you observe Mr. Deronjic's interactions with President Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you form any view as to whether they were on friendly terms or unfriendly terms?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, one got the impression that they were on friendly terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What gave you that impression?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, as he was being received and as they were saying goodbye.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Continue your answer, Mr. Ristic. What was it about when he was being received and saying goodbye that led you to form the impression that they were on friendly terms?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, they greeted each other cordially. When he was received, you could see that they were pleased, and also when they were saying goodbye. At least that's my impression. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, do you know the name Arkan?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you ever see President Karadzic and Arkan together?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: It was in Bijeljina in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What was the occasion?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, there was a review of that military unit, a military parade. And the president came to greet the parade, and I was on his security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the purpose of that parade?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, while the president was in Pale between April 1992 and the end of the conflict in late 1995, would he spend more of his time at his residence or would he spend more of his time at his cabinet?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: He spent more time at his office than at the residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was it the duty of your security detail to be kept informed of his whereabouts while he was in Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: While he was at his cabinet, what were his -- what would he generally be doing there, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, he was in meetings and performed other duties that arose.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Were the meetings with civilian or with military people?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Most of the meetings were with civilian people. But, of course, since he was the supreme commander, military officers came there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What kinds of civilian people would he hold meetings with?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: In the main, they were presidents of crisis staffs of various towns in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You've told the Court that towards the latter end of the conflict, you were assigned to the personal protection of the president; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you personally travel with the president if he was travelling outside Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Where would those trips go to, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Mostly, across Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you tell us a little more about that? Where, in particular, in Republika Srpska would he go?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: We would go to Zvornik, Bijeljina, Banja Luka, Trebinje, Bileca, Jajce, Mrkonjic, I mean Mrkonjic Grad, and so on, other places too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to call up now P2784, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: When this document arrives on your screen, you'll see that it's a communication dated the 3rd of August, 1995, which refers to a trip by President Karadzic to Srebrenica which was due to take place on the 4th of August, 1995. Now, I want to focus, first of all, on the addressees of this communication. We see the third addressee. Could you look at that, please, Mr. Ristic? It says: "Main Staff of the VRS - OB Sector."

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that: "GSS VRS OB Sector."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And what was the OB Sector?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I presume Intelligence and Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This trip, to the best of your knowledge, did it, in fact, take place, the trip to Srebrenica on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you accompany the president on that trip?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, you'll see the route described in this trip. I want you to -- just to focus on the route described. It's in the third paragraph down, and you'll see it says: "Pale to Sokolac." I want to note there's an error in the English translation. It should read "Pale to Sokolac." Anyway, Mr. Ristic, it says: "Pale-Sokolac-Han Pijesak-Vlasenica-Milici-Bratunac-Srebrenica." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was that the route that the convoy, in fact, took on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you omit Zvornik on purpose?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry. The route, Mr. President, does not refer to Zvornik. It says -- it should say: "Pale-Sokolac-Han Pijesak-Vlasenica-Milici-Bratunac-Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I read the wrong lines apparently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like you, Mr. Ristic, to help us understand this route.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And so I'd like to call up a map. That's 02227A. Can I suggest, Mr. President, that I provide Mr. Ristic with a hard copy of the map from which the electronic copy is taken so he can orient himself? The Defence has seen this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm providing Mr. Ristic with a portion of 65 ter 02227, and the version on the screen is a further smaller portion of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic, take your time on this, but if you could look at that map and see if you can identify the towns of Milici, Bratunac and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I inquire as to why we don't have the map from July 1995 without the military markings, because this map has nothing to do with that trip.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm simply asking the witness to mark the road route from Milici to Bratunac-Srebrenica. I won't be asking anything else about this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we're not taking anything else, other than the routing. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, can you -- have you found Milici, Bratunac and Srebrenica on that map? Did you hear my question, Mr. Ristic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've found them, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar to further enlarge the map just a little more. Thank you, that will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you take a pen and, with the Registrar's assistance, mark the road, the portion from -- the road as it comes in from Vlasenica to Milici to Bratunac to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait until -- is it okay, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's okay, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see Vlasenica on this map. I can only find Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark the route from Milici to Bratunac to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right. So this depicts the road as it comes in from Vlasenica to Milici, to Bratunac, to Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you sign and date that, please?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2843, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I call up, please, 65 ter 02062.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I suggest that the date of the 4th of August be written there, or perhaps we should have it in the transcript. What I'm concerned about is: Why should we have a map from July 1995 depicting a route that was taken on the 4th of August, 1995? I simply don't see why this military situation should be tied in with this trip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has taken your point, rest assured. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The document which will be appearing on our screens now is a communication from Beara, of the Intelligence and Security Sector of the Main Staff, to the Security Department of the Drina Corps, dated the 3rd of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, could you help us with the one thing here? Do you see, Mr. Ristic, that this is from the Intelligence and Security Sector of the Main Staff of the VRS? Would you like it to be blown up a little?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, please. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that the entity you referred to in the previous document?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. Could you repeat it or clarify it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I will, indeed. In the last document, I asked you about an entity described as the OB Sector of the Main Staff. Now, in this document, we see a reference to the Intelligence and Security Sector. That's on the second line of the top of the document. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is this the same entity that you described earlier, when I asked you what the OB Sector was?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: You mean the other dispatch that was sent to them? Yes, it was sent to them and to police stations, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Who was primarily responsible for the security of the president's convoy? Was it the police or was it the army?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: It was the police, the State Security Sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What, therefore, was the role of the army?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: From what I can read here, it seems that their role was to secure a stretch of the road and to report back any information, since the presence of a number of enemy groups was noted in the areas of Bratunac and Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This document, as you can see, refers to a trip on the 4th of August, 1995, by President Radovan Karadzic, and refers to the portion of the route from Sokolac to Han Pijesak to Vlasenica to Milici to Bratunac to Srebrenica. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Does this appear to be a reference to the same trip that we've been talking about that took place on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: That is the trip; no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that for admission, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor introduced this document as something written by Mr. Beara. Do you know his rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P2844, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to call up now, please, 02132, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, you've previously had the opportunity to look at this, Witness, and as we can see, it's scarcely legible in this form. And if we go to page 4, we'll see a handwritten version of it. If we can go to page 4, please. Page 3, possibly. Now, if you look at this document, towards the end of the paragraph which is paragraph 2, and just above paragraph 3, do you see that portion? It reads: "The president of Republika Srpska and the commander of the DK were in Srebrenica, in the brigade's area of responsibility, today."

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if we go back to the first page of the B/C/S version, and if we can keep the English. Could we enlarge, as much as possible, please, Mr. Registrar, the portion of the document that we've just been looking at, which is the bottom portion of paragraph 2. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think you can see, in the typewritten version as well, that there's a reference to the commander of the DK. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Truly, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can enlarge the last couple of words of the bottom of paragraph 2, Mr. Registrar. And I'd like to correct my words. Earlier, I said this was a typewritten version. It's not a typewritten version. It appears to be a teletyped version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If you can see it, say so. And if you can't, we can inspect it later and Their Honours will have that opportunity. Do you see the reference to the commander of the DK?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see the last line, as well as the "DK Commander," if that's what you're referring to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you happen to know who the commander of the Drina Corps -- of the DK was on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This refers to a trip, obviously, by the president, as well as the commander, to the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps on the 4th of August, 1995. Do you believe this to be a reference to the same trip that we've been referring to earlier?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I think it is the same trip. It was the only one. But I don't recall any commander of the Drina Corps being with us -- or, rather, being with the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P2845, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you bring up P2242, page 88 in English, page 102 in B/C/S. This is the appointment diary for President Karadzic for 1995. It's already in evidence. Mr. Registrar, could I have page 88 in English, page 102 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If you look at the first two lines of this page, Mr. Ristic, you see a reference to: "4th of the 8th, 1995, 0900 - Srebrenica - visit." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is that consistent with what you have told us earlier about the visit to Srebrenica on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, we won't be looking at any more documents, Mr. Ristic. Thank you. What did you do at Srebrenica when you arrived there on that day, the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, we attended the erection of a cross on a nearby hilltop. It was more of a religious ceremony. I don't really know what it was really about because I was preoccupied with security issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you go into the centre of the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, as we were passing through, we did stop for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What did you do in the centre of the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: We visited an Orthodox Church, the one in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the visit to the church?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, we went to see the site, and we found it completely destroyed. And we realised that the enemy forces had been keeping their chickens there while they were staying in the area. You could tell by the excrements that were left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was the church, in fact, destroyed, was it completely destroyed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, you could only tell that it was a church by its contours. It was completely devastated. Otherwise, there was no icons, no frescoes, everything was destroyed, but the walls were still standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic, not limited to that church, you said a while ago that when you -- let me find it. Yes. You simply went to see the site, referring to Srebrenica, and: "... we found it completely destroyed." Could you describe to us, as much as possible in detail, the degree it was destroyed, the destruction? Could you do that? The degree of destruction of Srebrenica town, as much as you can remember now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as I was passing through Srebrenica, my impression was that it wasn't that destroyed or at all; perhaps only in the areas close to the confrontation lines, where fighting was going on. But in the town proper, it was not -- there was no destruction at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But when you said, in line 19: "Well, quite simply, we went to see the site, and we found it completely destroyed," could you clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the church and the grounds around the church.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you see a mosque or a minaret in the centre of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No. I don't remember, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was there any comment within the party that you were with as to any destruction of a mosque in Srebrenica town or in the environs of Srebrenica town?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Leading and suggesting something that the witness did not confirm. The witness did not confirm that the mosque was destroyed. He said that he didn't recall seeing anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The point has been taken by Mr. Gaynor. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll move on, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At the religious ceremony, you refer to a cross. Was it a blessing of a cross or was it a blessing of something else?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, my personal impression was that this was planned to be a monumental site, like a memorial complex, and it was more of the consecration of the ground, rather than anything else. At any rate, it was a religious ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ristic, you will be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Ristic.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to make a pause between my question and your answer, and that applies to me as well, in order for everything to be entered into the transcript. For example, on page 32, line 22, it was recorded that you said that chickens were being kept in the church. Is it true that this is what you said, that domestic animals were kept there, and that according to the dung found there, that included cattle and other animals, not only chickens?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: It is quite true that I said that there was cattle, but I never mentioned chickens. And I concluded that based on the dung found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: It concerns this critical day in Sarajevo. Is it true that on the 4th and 5th of April, you were on duty securing the premises of the Serbian Democratic Party at Holiday Inn Hotel?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that my family, whom you escorted via Vraca, left Sarajevo at the 11th hour, virtually, under the hail of bullets?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember me sitting in the hall of the Holiday Inn and waiting for Mr. Izetbegovic so that both of us could go to a television studio, and also Mr. Kljuic from the HDZ was to join us, in order to appeal to the people, via television, to preserve peace and to try and prevent war?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I know that you appeared on television with these gentlemen that you mentioned. Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that on that occasion, I gave an interview to Novi Sad TV, Milijana Baletic, the journalist, who recorded my meeting with Muhamed Cengic whilst we were waiting for Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I know this female journalist. I know that she was there. And I know that you gave an interview to her, but I don't know what about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that my security detail did not allow me to go back to Holiday Inn, but they escorted me from the TV studio to Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the morning of the 5th, while we were still at Holiday Inn, my flat was fired at from a machine-gun, and that after that it was looted and demolished, and that all our valuables, clothes, and other belongings were still there, that not a single item had been removed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that, and I personally saw this footage. I believe that this footage was made by Mr. Mirko Caberlo [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They're having a problem with this last name. Do you remember that until the very last moment, we hoped that war wouldn't break out, and for that reason we did not evacuate either the archive of the SDS or our family belongings from my family flat, and that we virtually fled the town just to save our lives at the last minute?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that this evacuation was urgent and quick and that there was no time for any extensive preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that even before that, we did not remove anything that belonged to us anywhere and that we did not believe that we should leave Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, nothing was evacuated beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After you have escorted my family, through the fighting that was in Vraca already underway, you continued to Holiday Inn to continue your duty on the premises of the Serbian Democratic Party and to keep an eye on Professor Aleksa Buha and the journalist Baletic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, among other things. There were other people there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you accompanied by Branko Kovacevic, also an official in the party and some other people, but was there anyone present there from the police, except you, who were actually working for our political party?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I was captured alongside Vlado Ilic, who was also a security officer from the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There was Miroslav Karabatov [phoen] there as well, but I don't know which position he held, and also Branko Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that you had coffee with the journalist and the hotel staff, and that in the meantime, a huge crowd of people gathered between Holiday Inn and the Assembly building of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that at one point this crowd burst into the hotel?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We were in the office of the deputy manager of the hotel. That was Milan Jevtic at the time. He was there on the premises, and Milijana Baletic, the journalist, and other members of the staff were there as well. We were just having coffee when this happened, when these people burst in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Prior to that, did any of the Serbs fire, did you have sniper rifles or marksmen, or was there any activity conducted by the Serbs from inside the hotel, Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: We were there just to provide security. There were no snipers, and none of the Serbs opened fire. We didn't notice anyone bearing arms in the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that you mention Vlado Ilic being armed, is it true that the first seven people from my security detail were assigned to me from the joint MUP -- or by the joint MUP, and that before the Special Brigade of the JNA was disbanded, had been at the JNA and then were transferred to the MUP of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of April or in May, you were admitted into the MUP of Republika Srpska. Is it true that a vetting procedure was conducted on that occasion and that you had received clearance, and that applied to everyone who wanted to work in the Security Department?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's true. I was checked, both physically and mentally, and I passed all these tests.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not recorded here that your pass was also checked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go back for a moment to Holiday Inn. This crowd burst in and asked you to surrender. Vlado Ilic asked, Who do we surrender to, counting that he was a policeman and that they were just a mob?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they arrive there in any official capacity? Did they resemble police officers or members of the military, or were they resembling a mob, more than that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: They resembled anything but any organised unit either from the police or the military. They resembled a mob, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When Ilic, being a police officer, refused to surrender, is it true that they threw a grenade into your room?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you managed to hurdle this grenade back into the corridor and that it exploded there on the spot?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And at that point, did they start shooting from the top of the surrounding buildings at your room from outside, through the windows?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes. After a while, they started shooting, and bullets started coming through the window of the office where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you captured there and taken to prison?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: We were captured. And after we had been tortured, they took us to a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Describe this torture for us.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Physical abuse, beatings, psychological torture with lots of foul language, humiliation, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that this was not a proper arrest, but, rather, a lynch?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: We would have been lynched had not the rest of the special unit, made up of Muslim and Croat special police officers, had come and rescued us from being lynched by this crowd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How did you personally fare through this torture?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Horribly. It was difficult. When I was captured, it was discovered that 12 of my ribs were broken, I was bruised, and the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were detained at the Public Security Station at Logavina. Were you beaten there as well?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they force you to sing certain songs there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which songs?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, mainly the songs that are characteristic of the Muslim people and that denote them, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many other Serbs were with you in the prison in Logavina?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd just like to note this appears to be along the lines of tu quoque evidence. The evidence being elicited, in our submission, is not particularly of assistance to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I tend to agree. And it's time to move on to another topic, Mr. Karadzic. Do you have any observation, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This is an incident for which -- the sniping of protesters at the Holiday Inn, for which the Serbs have been blamed for that, and I believe there has been some evidence already that -- in our trial, that that was the part of the beginning of the war where the Serbs were sniping from the SDS contingent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understand, so that's why I let it go for some time. But a detailed description I don't think will assist the Chamber in such a detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So after that, you were exchanged, you were medically treated, your past was checked, and then you were employed by the police and assigned to secure the facility where I and my family lived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Villa Sipad was mentioned here. Am I right if I say that it was a very bad and poor building and that this villa in no way could be described as a luxurious building? This was a very small weekend cottage?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. We just called it that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that there were frequent power cuts, and that even if the generator was working, due to the lack of electricity, I had difficulty in communicating with somebody else elsewhere in the country?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: It is true that there was electricity cut off quite often. I don't know what problems you had with communication systems, but I know that communication links were severed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the radio set that Mr. Gaynor asked you about was used by you within the range of five kilometres in order to keep you abreast of my movements, whether I was going to the Assembly or to attend a meeting?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it served for security purposes, and it covered these radios at Pale and it provided contact with your security. We were in touch with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that we could not communicate with Sokolac or Sarajevo via this radio set, let alone other places in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Today, on page 18, you were asked about meetings with military personnel from the Army of Republika Srpska. Do you remember that military personnel, including Mladic and Gvero and commanders of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, on their route from Lukavica to Han Pijesak and back, had to pass through Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had to on this particular section.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that quite a few of these meetings were just a matter of courtesy, they stopped by to greet me?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my impression. I would agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you knew that from August 1994 until the end of the war, the relationships between the civilian and military structures were frosty and disrupted?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 21, you were asked about Mr. Deronjic. Do you agree that Mr. Deronjic never came to see me privately, but that he always came as a representative of municipal authorities? So is it true that Mr. Deronjic ever visited me at my home or not?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't remember him visiting you at your home, and I really couldn't think of any reason why that should have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Mr. Deronjic was a student of Professor Koljevic and that they were acquaintances rather than with me?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that I know much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice that I received anyone in a cold fashion, or was I courteous and polite towards everyone, including Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: You were kind and polite towards everyone. You received them cordially.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You had an opportunity, weren't you [as interpreted], to see me receiving representatives of the international community? Were these meetings also amicable and cordial and always ended with a lunch?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, for the most part, just as you described.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we then agree that Mr. Deronjic was not given any better or worse reception than anyone else who came to see me?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree on that. I said that he was received by you in a cordial manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 23, you were asked today something about Arkan and my encounters with him. Do you agree that you never saw me having any contact with Arkan either before or after that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was just that one encounter. That's as far as my knowledge goes. And I was present there when you met him as I described.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that a military ceremony that involved the lining up of units that had returned from the region of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you started travelling with me, did you accompany me on my trips to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice or did somebody told [as interpreted] you that in Belgrade, I had contacts with Mr. Arkan?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No, I did not notice that, and I never heard of you having any contact with Arkan during your stay there, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find out or did you see for yourself that I communicated with him over the phone? Did he ever call me or did I ever call him whilst you were with me?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't know that there were any contacts?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that there were any contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did my friends, like Nogo, Djogo, Brana Crncevic, Momo Kapor and others come to my home?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Those are mostly authors, artists, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, the ones that you mentioned are mostly writers, poets, painters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, talking about my travels, did you ever see or hear that I ever went to a casino to gamble?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: That never happened while I was with you, nor do I know anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that I asked you, who were on my security detail, a dozen of you, I always asked you to be modest and to always treat citizens and everyone else with whom you come into contact in a civilised and polite manner?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I acted accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that I did not expect you to be involved in anything else, other than providing security, and that all of you were worse off, in terms of wealth, after the war than you were before the war?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA RISTIC
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
